reason: The cited evidence directly supports the formation of coherent L12 precipitates from Ti additions in FCC HEAs (E1), the thermal stability and strength retention of γ/γ′ HEAs at ~800 °C (E2), and the dominance of precipitation hardening (E1). However, the specific Ti–Ni primary composition (Ti35Ni35Al10Cr10Co10) and the precise 20% yield strength increase at 800 °C are not directly tested in the cited passages, representing a minor overstatement.
premises: Ti addition to FCC HEAs can form coherent L12-type precipitates (e.g., (Ni,Co)3Ti) that provide significant precipitation strengthening.
γ/γ′ microstructures in HEAs with Al+Ti exhibit excellent thermal stability and strength retention around 800 °C.
Precipitation hardening from L12 phases is much greater than solid solution hardening in these alloy systems.
Coherent, low-misfit precipitates can strengthen without severely degrading ductility.
